questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Authorization”?
options: Authorization should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Authorization helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Authorization means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Authorization removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Authorization helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Authorization is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Roles and permissions” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Roles and permissions” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Roles and permissions” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Roles and permissions” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Roles and permissions” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Roles and permissions” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Roles and permissions” under Authorization. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Authorization”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
